page: Vultr voc-g-40c-160gb-768s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server built on the AMD EPYC processor platform using the x86_64 architecture. The instance delivers 40 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 20 physical cores running at a base clock frequency of 2.0 GHz, supporting simultaneous multithreading with two threads per core. System resources include 160 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware provisioning also bundles 768 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage without standalone GPU acceleration, alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance consistently in the top tier for memory throughput, yielding uncached read bandwidth of 451.84 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 262.45 GB/sec. Multi-core performance metrics are equally robust, registering strong results in PassMark CPU tests (72,888.75) and stress-ng multi-core testing (123,693.48). Parallel compilation using Clang and multi-threaded decompression tests reflect rapid execution under heavy concurrency. In-memory operations demonstrate notable efficiency, producing 84.31 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks, while single-core metrics across Geekbench and compression tasks align with median expectations for 2.0 GHz EPYC architectures.

With dedicated CPU threads and a symmetrical balance between compute cores and memory capacity, the instance offers predictable execution without virtualization contention or CPU throttling. The absence of AVX-512 extensions and discrete GPU accelerators limits its viability for specialized matrix math and ultra-large deep learning pipelines. However, the combination of high uncached memory bandwidth, local NVMe storage, and dense multi-core processing makes this server well matched for multi-threaded build farms, Redis caching tiers, relational database engines, and medium-scale LLM inference pipelines.
description: Vultr voc-g-40c-160gb-768s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor. The configuration provisions 40 dedicated vCPUs across 20 physical cores operating at 2.0 GHz, 160 GB of system memory, and 768 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, operating without dedicated GPU hardware. With a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, it demonstrates solid multi-threaded computational power, highlighted by strong results in PassMark CPU benchmarks, stress-ng multi-core evaluations, and high Redis write throughput. Its memory subsystem demonstrates top-tier large-block read and write bandwidth, offsetting median single-core frequencies. The lack of hardware accelerators or AVX-512 instructions restricts dense AI training, yet the dedicated core allocation and fast NVMe storage ensure predictable performance. This instance is suited for multi-threaded software compilation, enterprise databases, in-memory caching clusters, and backend web serving.
